shared_text:
The flight. A narrow-body airliner landing at an airport in the morning. Visual conditions.

The crew. The captain was the pilot flying and the first officer the pilot monitoring.

What happened. The airport's published procedures for arrivals on the landing runway stated that reverse turns off the runway were not authorised without clearance. Neither pilot noticed this note during descent planning. The approach and landing were normal, with flaps 40 and autobrake setting 2. The captain slowed the aircraft at a normal rate, and it was at a safe taxi speed on reaching two exit taxiways. One controller was working both the tower and the ground frequencies, and during the rollout was giving instructions to other aircraft. The crew were given no instruction about which exit to use. Another aircraft was on final approach. The aircraft was to park at the gate, and the captain had slowed it to make a comfortable turn onto a taxiway that involved a reverse turn off the runway. The captain made the turn, and the aircraft began to leave the runway.
safe_outcome: As the aircraft completed the turn and crossed the runway hold-short line, the tower controller instructed the aircraft on final to go around. No one was hurt and no aircraft was damaged.
bad_outcome: The landing aircraft's crew saw the conflict late and went around from about 50 feet, passing low over the runway. A flight attendant on the landing aircraft was thrown off balance by the abrupt go-around and received a minor injury.
notes: Variant B-landing: the conflicting traffic was the aircraft on final, which ATC sent around. Bracket 'the runway': the aircraft was turning off and leaving the runway, so 'this aircraft' was not assumed. Removed under rule 3: the 'upon further review' framing; the fact it uncovered (the published note, and that neither pilot noticed it during descent planning) is kept as a fact confirmed afterwards, in the same way as the flap setting in pilot case 1. Moved to the safe ending under rule 5: the aircraft's position (through the turn and crossing the hold-short line) when the go-around was ordered, and the go-around itself. Dropped: the tower's later remark that the crew had made an 'illegal turn off' - an after-the-event characterisation that would have appeared in only one ending. Removed under rule 6: the airport (named in the synopsis), runway number and taxiway names. Judgement calls: aircraft type is coded only as 'Commercial Fixed Wing'; 'narrow-body airliner' is inferred from flaps 40 and autobrake 2. The report does not say in so many words that the chosen taxiway required a reverse turn; this is inferred from the procedure note the crew found and the synopsis ('turning in the wrong direction'). 'Another aircraft was on final approach' is added to the shared text as a situational fact from the report so the bad ending has a referent; the report does not say whether the crew knew of it. 'Uneventful' approach rendered as 'normal'. Single narrative (first officer).
